subject: Sizing for Stratagem Dedicated Capacity and Burst Strategy
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan@stratagem.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratagem.ai
Date: 2027-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing request + SLA targets

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Stratagem's product team is ready to move from pilot to a committed Dedicated plan, but we need a concrete sizing recommendation for the deal team and procurement. Attaching our short workload profile (stratagem_workload_profile.csv). Key asks:

- p95 latency target: <= 300ms for standard chat flows (streaming acceptable)
- Peak traffic pattern: bursty daily peak windows (30–45 minutes) with occasional minute-long spikes
- Expected growth: 20% monthly token growth first quarter after launch

Can you provide a recommended GPU slab (type + count), an explanation for headroom and fallback strategy (model variants), and an initial committed capacity suggestion (monthly GPU-hours)? Procurement would like a ballpark cost estimate before the legal review.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of AI, Stratagem AI

Attachments: stratagem_workload_profile.csv (CSV, 14KB)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan@stratagem.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request + SLA targets

Hi Evan —

Got the profile, thanks. We're happy to size this out. A couple quick clarifying questions before we lock down numbers so we don't under/over-provision:

1) Avg request distribution: do you have an estimate for average tokens per request (prompt + response) across the majority of traffic? Your CSV had percentiles but not a clear avg — rough number is fine.
2) % of requests that require long context (>4k tokens) vs short context (<1k).
3) Can you tolerate occasional higher-latency (graceful fallback) responses for rare long-context requests, or do all requests need the same p95?
4) Are you open to a hybrid model approach (13B quantized for bulk traffic, 70B for high-quality / agent flows) to lower overall GPU needs?

I looped in Ben and Priyom; Ben will run a capacity model with conservative p95 throughput profiles once we have (1) and (2). We'll aim to deliver a recommended slab + a 12-month commit suggestion by next Friday.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-14T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Stratagem sizing calc + recommended slab (draft)

Mateo / Priyom —

I've run the draft numbers based on the CSV and Evan's clarification call (they confirmed avg tokens/request ~150, approx 75 RPS peak inside short burst windows, ~8% long-context). Assumptions and conservative safety margins below; this is intended for the proposal packet.

Assumptions
- Avg tokens per request (prompt + response): 150 tokens
- Peak RPS during burst: 75 requests/sec
- Peak tokens/sec (T/s) = 75 * 150 = 11,250 T/s
- Target headroom: 30% (for growth + burst protection) => design T/s = 11,250 * 1.3 = 14,625 T/s
- Long-context (~8%) routed to a larger model (70B-class) with lower throughput; rest handled on 13B-class quantized runtimes.

Throughput per GPU (p95 conservative estimates, streaming enabled)
- 13B quantized (q4* on A100-class): ~4,500 T/s per GPU
- 70B quantized (q4* on A100-class): ~1,600 T/s per GPU

Sizing math (primary plan = 13B-first with 70B fallback)
- Required 13B GPU count for bulk traffic: ceil(14,625 / 4,500) = 4 GPUs -> but add N+1 redundancy => 5 GPUs dedicated to 13B traffic
- Long-context capacity (8% of traffic): 14,625 * 0.08 = 1,170 T/s -> require ceil(1,170 / 1,600) = 1 GPU for the 70B path; add 1 for redundancy => 2 GPUs for 70B
- Minimum operational slab per this model: 7 GPUs (5x13B + 2x70B)

Operational considerations & recommended slab sizing
- Recommend provisioning an initial dedicated slab of 10 A100-class GPUs. Why 10? It gives:
  * N+1 coverage for maintenance and QOS (the 7 above + 3 spare for canary/cold-starts/burst offload)
  * Room for a canary node and a small GPU pool for heavy agent tasks that might spike without impacting bulk chat flows
  * Buffer for 20% month-1 growth and safety while we monitor actual utilization

Optimizations that materially reduce required GPUs
- KV/prefix caching and prompt templating: 15–25% reduction in effective token compute on typical chat patterns — we used a conservative 18% reduction when sizing; if Stratagem can adopt more aggressive caching this could drop required 13B GPUs from 5 -> 4.
- Batching in the runtime for short requests: improves per-GPU throughput on A100 by ~10–15% during sustained windows; plan on enabling adaptive batching.

Latency / SLO fit
- With the recommended slab and streaming enabled, we project p95 serving latency ~220–280ms for 13B-class flows (measured from first byte to last token streamed) under burst conditions. The 70B fallback path will have higher p95 (~350–450ms) for long-context flows — recommend signaling that to Stratagem and using 70B for quality-critical endpoints only.

Commit guidance (ballpark for procurement)
- Suggested starting commit: 10 GPUs reserved, 12-month term. We will propose a burst allowance to use extra hosted capacity in rare spikes.
- Estimate: commit pricing + typical usage pattern yields an estimated monthly bill in the attached spreadsheet (stratagem_proposal_v2.xlsx). Exact numbers depend on exact GPU SKU and burst policy; procurement can use this as a baseline for negotiation.

Next steps
1) Mateo to review and produce an external-facing one-page slab recommendation (with the two-model hybrid story and a fallback flow chart).
2) Share the proposal pack with Stratagem, schedule a 30-min procurement alignment to confirm commit and burst language.

Notes: these numbers are conservative and assume no aggressive model distillation or further quantization beyond q4-style runtimes. If they allow smaller-context cutoffs and more caching we can materially reduce the reserved footprint.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: procurement@stratagem.ai, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-17T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request + SLA targets

Evan —

Thanks for the profile and for the call. Attached is a concise recommendation and the draft proposal packet (stratagem_proposal_v2.xlsx) — Ben's internal sizing is summarized below so you have the quick answer for procurement:

- Recommended starting dedicated slab: 10 A100-class GPUs (hybrid: majority 13B quantized runtime, small 70B pool for long-context/agent flows)
- Design throughput target (with 30% headroom): ~14.6k tokens/sec
- Operational breakdown: 5 GPUs sized for bulk 13B traffic (N+1 included), 2 GPUs for 70B fallback, 3 spare for canary/maintenance/burst offload
- Expected p95: 220–280ms for the 13B path; 350–450ms for long-context 70B requests
- Optimizations we will enable from day one: KV/prefix caching, adaptive batching, and request routing by latency/cost policy

Procurement note: we recommend a 12-month reserved commitment on the 10-GPU slab with a documented burst policy to fall back to hosted capacity for rare tails. Pricing ballpark and exact GPU SKU options are in the attached spreadsheet.

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-minute procurement sync on Tuesday (2027-04-20) to confirm commit levels and contract language? If procurement wants to shave costs immediately, we can supply a quick sensitivity plan showing how caching + shifting 20% of long-context to async jobs reduces the slab to 8 GPUs (and the associated pricing).

If that sounds good I will send over the formal proposal and a short diagram that shows routing + fallback.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference

Attachments: stratagem_proposal_v2.xlsx (Excel, 42KB); gpu_throughput_notes.pdf (PDF, 38KB)
